identity.worldRole: A temporary, deliberately understandable interruption in the enemy route that turns path control into a visible player-authored hypothesis.
identity.manufactureContext: Built rapidly in the fortress workshop from standardized structural modules intended to be repaired, replaced and visibly tested under pressure.
identity.emotionalIntent: Dependable and brave without appearing invulnerable; its damage should create urgency and useful concern rather than helplessness.
identity.territoryVisualThesis: A dependable standardized lane-blocking chassis whose single replaced panel and diagonal brace make prior survival memorable without weakening its broad mobile silhouette.

instantRead.oneSecondPromise: This broad grounded object blocks a lane now, shows where it is weakening, and can be understood before the next enemy reaches it.
instantRead.orientationCue: The reinforced presentation face addresses incoming enemies; the flatter service face and interaction light address the player.
instantRead.interactionCue: A complete, waist-height service socket or status module is readable from the safe rear side.
instantRead.dangerCue: Breaks, tilted panels and exposed structure progress from one localized weakness to a wide critical breach.
instantRead.relationToPlayer: Friendly player-built infrastructure that invites repair and repositioning rather than fear.

proportionRules: The full width remains exactly twice the height and four times the depth.
The two feet occupy the outer thirds and keep a clear central ground gap.
The blocking panels occupy most of the frontal area while the frame remains the silhouette authority.
The interaction module stays above the player's ground clutter and below the top rail.

views.front: A wide low fortress gate fragment: two planted feet, two outer posts, strong top and bottom rails, and three readable blocking bays facing the enemy.
views.back: A calmer service plane with visible frame continuity, repair access and the interaction module; it must never resemble the enemy-facing impact side.
views.left: A compact planted wedge showing the foot depth, post thickness and credible connection between panel, rail and ground contact.
views.right: The mirrored functional profile with only approved territory asymmetry; no cable, plate or damage fragment may float outside the structural chain.
views.top: A shallow defensive bar with two stable footprints and a clear front-to-back distinction created by impact armor versus service mass.
views.bottom: Only grounded feet, underslung rail structure and intentional clearances are visible; no decorative underside detail consumes budget.
views.threeQuarterFront: The canonical hero read combines broad blocking silhouette, panel rhythm, planted feet and the enemy-facing reinforcement logic.
views.threeQuarterBack: The service read exposes repair logic and interaction access while preserving the same outer silhouette and footprint.
views.gameCamera: From elevated third-person mobile view, the object reads as one broad lane blocker with three state-readable bays, not as a pile of small parts.

artDirection.territoryThesis: A hopeful fortress culture of intelligent survival: calm standardized chassis make every tool dependable, while one or two visible adaptations turn scarcity, repair and shared history into proud authorship without post-apocalyptic noise.
shapeGrammar: large protected apertures and explicit load-bearing joints
one localized offset brace or replacement module
visible replacement, reinforcement, sealing or rerouting logic
artDirection.exaggeration: Function, load paths, service access and the single authored adaptation are enlarged enough to read on mobile; distress, dirt and tiny mechanics never carry identity.
artDirection.edgeLanguage: Large consistent structural bevels create calm readable highlights; only the boundary of an approved repair may use a sharper cut or visibly renewed edge, and nothing becomes razor-thin.
artDirection.detailDensity: Low secondary construction density and extremely low tertiary density; seventy-two percent primary mass, twenty-three percent functional secondary structure and five percent causal finish.
artDirection.asymmetry: Twenty-four-percent controlled asymmetry expresses adaptation inside a seventy-five-to-eighty-five-percent standardized chassis; footprint, facing, collision promise, pivots and gameplay anchors remain fixed.
artDirection.materialLanguage: Deep coated structure, reclaimed composite panels, exposed durable metal, matte contacts and rare contextual wood surround carefully protected interaction technology.
artDirection.paletteLogic: Deep slate and bone-sand create a quiet frontier base; sun-baked copper identifies player intervention, while mint interaction, raspberry threat, gold warning and red critical remain bounded semantic roles.
artDirection.surfaceTreatment: Broad calm planes, one or two patch boundaries and directional abrasion tell a construction history without uniform grime, material roulette or photoreal texture chatter.
artDirection.wearLogic: Every scar must name a cause: prior impact, heat, hand contact, ground abrasion or an approved repair operation; damage widens one causal chain and repair reverses it.

forbidden: decorative repair with no causal reason
